newsitem.title: RUSSIA: MFK, Renaissance form Russia's largest investment bank.
newsitem.headline: MFK, Renaissance form Russia's largest investment bank.

text.p: Russia's Bank MFK merged with Renaissance Capital, forming Russia's single largest investment bank, the companies said Wednesday.

MFK-Renaissance, which has hopes of international stature but plans to concentrate on the Russian market, will have $400 million in equity capital, total assets of $2 billion and a further $1 billion under management, the companies said.
"This has the possibility of becoming a bank of world stature," Boris Jordan, chief executive of the new company, said.
Officials said the new bank would work independently from the powerful Unexim-MFK financial industrial company that owns half of the new company and will provide a large chunk of its work.

"The Renaissance group has positive control over the company," said Jordan, previously head of Renaissance Capital. MFK, also known as ICFI, and Renaissance shareholders each own 50 percent of the merged company.

Renaissance Capital and Bank MFK are both active in trading and issuing Russian securities and corporate finance. The central bank said recently that Uneximbank was Russia's third largest bank by assets and Bank MFK was 15th.
Russian former First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin will be chairman of the new company.
